sources.title: The Declaration of Independence of the United States of America
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright Status line: Public domain in the USA
sources.needIt: The founding promise of the country, short enough to read in five minutes.
sources.notes: Short primary text, a good opener. Note what it left out about who counted.

sources.title: The Federalist Papers
sources.by: Alexander Hamilton, John Jay and James Madison
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright Status line: Public domain in the USA
sources.needIt: Why the Constitution was built the way it was: separate powers, factions, checks.
sources.notes: Long and dense; use 3 or 4 key essays and rewrite in plain English.

sources.title: Common Sense
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright Status line: Public domain in the USA
sources.needIt: A short pamphlet that moved ordinary people; shows how plain words change history.
sources.notes: Short and punchy. A good first reading.

sources.title: The Autobiography of Benjamin Franklin
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright Status line: Public domain in the USA
sources.needIt: A self-made citizen's habits of thrift, learning and public service.
sources.notes: Use the self-improvement chapters. Some period attitudes on religion and race need framing.

sources.title: Democracy in America, Volume 1
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright Status line: Public domain in the USA
sources.needIt: A foreign visitor's sharp read of American habits: clubs, equality, majority pressure.
sources.notes: Long and old-fashioned; short extracts only. Has period views on race and Native people that a builder must frame.

sources.title: Utopia
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright Status line: Public domain in the USA
sources.needIt: A thought experiment on how a society could be run differently.
sources.notes: Satirical; best as a discussion starter for older students.
